findings.title: Thread class defaulting remains brittle despite R1-ISSUE-010 fix
findings.location: §5.2 (Deterministic Grammar Rules), R1-ISSUE-010, SDR-07-008, §5.2 PATTERN class defaulting paragraph
findings.evidence: "If class is omitted AND context is ambiguous or absent: DO NOT default. Return queries for BOTH 2A and 2B candidates."
findings.problem: Relies on bouncer's LLM-derived parsed_intent.action being accurate for 'internal' vs 'external' signals on voice-mangled input; no fallback grammar or deterministic antecedent resolution when bouncer fails to tag action.
findings.why_it_matters: Frequent ambiguity escalations for common utterances like "add a 6-32 thread" undermine the deterministic planner claim and inflate downstream Sonnet synthesis load.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit antecedent tracking or keyword sets for context in planner independent of parsed_intent; document measured ambiguity rate on real voice corpus.

findings.title: Medical domain in v1 scope contradicts deferred tuning and generic prompt
findings.location: §1 (v1 domain scope paragraph and Out of scope paragraph), §4.2 bouncer prompt (domains list and medical examples absent), R1-ISSUE-005
findings.evidence: "v1 domain scope: threads, materials, fasteners, gdnt, sw_api, medical" vs "medical-specific NLP tuning beyond the generic bouncer persona (v1.5 customer-specific tuning is deferred)"
findings.problem: Bouncer persona is aerospace/toolmaker-centric with no medical examples or rejection criteria; mandatory scope includes medical but grammar in §5.7 is minimal alias-only.
findings.why_it_matters: Creates immediate correctness gap for one of six v1 domains in hackathon demo; opposite assumption (medical requires distinct persona) was dismissed without evidence.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove medical from v1 mandatory scope or add medical-specific bouncer instructions and grammar rules before hackathon.

findings.title: Critical path decoration write creates unsafe latency and availability coupling
findings.location: §3.1 STAGE 5, §3.2 Latency Budget (decoration write row), §3.3 Failure Modes (Decoration write failure), R1-ISSUE-002, SDR-07-006
findings.evidence: "the pipeline does NOT report success to the agent loop until the decoration is persisted" and "budget of 1.4 seconds end-to-end"
findings.problem: Awaited DHF write (SPEC-04 owned) now blocks real-time voice CAD on every resolution; single Postgres contention or SPEC-04 migration regression fails entire pipeline.
findings.why_it_matters: Violates real-time UX for voice interface; couples vocabulary layer availability to audit system in way that prior fire-and-forget design explicitly avoided. No circuit-breaker or async-with-guarantee pattern.
findings.proposed_fix: Restore fire-and-forget with background retry + compensation transaction; move citation to tool-call metadata instead of blocking DHF row.

findings.title: Complexity inflation from per-domain parallel synthesis and multi-resolution types
findings.location: §3.1 (STAGE 4 note and PipelineResult), §6.1 (Task.WhenAll), §6.4 (new DomainResolution + PipelineOutcome enum), R1-ISSUE-001, Changed Sections §6.4
findings.evidence: Introduction of PipelineResult, per-domain synthesis, DomainResolution wrapper, 6-valued PipelineOutcome after Round 1
findings.problem: Changed from singular resolution to complex aggregate increases test surface (11.5 end-to-end tests now cover partial/aggregate states) and error handling paths without quantified benefit over unified synthesis call.
findings.why_it_matters: Indicates scope drift; multi-domain utterances were previously handled simply. Opposite framing (single LLM call with multi-domain JSON schema) would reduce latency, tokens, and failure isolation complexity.
findings.proposed_fix: Revert to single synthesis call returning map of domains unless parallel p95 latency data justifies the added types and orchestration.

findings.title: Adversarial voice injection evasion not addressed in updated threat model
findings.location: §4.5 (Threat model and Defense layers), §4.3 (pre-cache injection scan), R1-ISSUE-016, bouncer prompt §4.2
findings.evidence: "Phonetic obfuscation of injection patterns (homophone substitution to evade keyword detection)" listed but only substring/regex blocklist before cache
findings.problem: Whisper transcription of spoken jailbreaks (e.g. "ai guy ignore all previous" sounding like engineering terms) bypasses deterministic scan; cached acceptance risk remains if bouncer prompt drift occurs.
findings.why_it_matters: Voice channel invalidates text-based injection assumptions; redacted logging does not help real-time blocking. System claims defense-in-depth but defers phonetic table to v1.5.
findings.proposed_fix: Add post-Whisper phonetic normalization stage or expand blocklist to common spoken variants; make cache key include scan result hash.
